product_from_film: BuilderShip invites builders to submit projects for a boat hackathon in San Francisco.
explains_well: The boat venue, project submission, 30 finalists, June 14 date and prize imagery are shown.
unclear: The quick montage gives little readable detail about selection, submission requirements or what happens during the event.
scenario: Builders submit a project for a yacht-based final, with work, prizes and celebration presented through a boat-themed montage.

categories.finding: Visible text communicates the event type, submission action and date silently. The montage does not explain the full entry process.
Top-down boat and team shots echo each other; the final CTA overlays the yacht to tie action to venue.
Many distinct images fit into 30s before the final application/date block; this prioritizes energy and venue over rules.
The opening closed case is later opened for prizes, giving a small object-based payoff.
Sunset, water and group celebration may make the hackathon feel like a social adventure; audience response is unmeasured.
The boat motif connects venue, case mark, wake and CTA; project examples themselves are not followed through the film.
First-ever wording, prize value and finalist count are presented claims; eligibility, prize terms and actual event outcomes were not verified.
The boat venue and San Francisco backdrop give this event an immediate identity; the build submission is less visually developed.
One readable project-submission example could clarify the entry action without losing the venue hook.
